title: Hospices before the surge: the California middle in 2015 and 2016
question: What did the typical California hospice look like in 2015 and 2016, before the Bay Area agencies in the hospice case were licensed?
finding: With one measure for every year (discharges other than death, over all discharges), the California middle hospice discharged 24% of its patients alive in 2015 and 26% in 2016, against 35% in 2019 and 37% in 2021 (the later forms drop this table; on the diagnosis table used for the case the middle went from 35% in 2019 to 48% in 2025). 12% of 2015 discharges came after 180 days or more. Hospices filing a report: 661 in 2015 (53 in the Bay Area), 1637 in 2025 (110). None of the case hospices is in the 2015 or 2016 files. A Plus Hospice, Inc. (2016: 20 patients), a separate licence in the same Pleasanton building as A Plus Prime Care, does appear.
how: HCAI home-health and hospice utilization files: 2015 and 2016 (complete data sets, sections 5-7), 2019 to 2025 (the nursing lane's cache of the same files). A hospice is a report with hospice discharges; medians over reports with at least 20 discharges. "Alive (by diagnosis table)" repeats the measure used by screen hospice-state-utilization for 2019-2025, which the 2015-16 forms do not have.
limits: The 2015-16 forms have only the discharges-by-reason table, and the 2022-25 forms (as cached) only the diagnosis table, so the two columns overlap in 2019-21 only; the 2015-16 figures compare with the "by reason" column, not with the 48.1% quoted in the case. A rise in live discharges can reflect stricter federal review of long stays, more dementia patients (who live longer), or better reporting.

sources.t: HCAI, Home Health Agency and Hospice Annual Utilization Data, complete data sets 2015 and 2016
